namespace.name: get_azure_bestpractices
namespace.title: Azure Best Practices
namespace.description:
Azure best practices - Commands return a list of best practices for code generation, operations and deployment when working with Azure services. It should be called for any code generation, deployment or operations involving Azure, Azure Functions, Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS), Azure Container Apps (ACA), Bicep, Terraform, Azure Cache, Redis, CosmosDB, Entra, Azure Active Directory, Azure App Services, or any other Azure technology or programming language. This command set also includes the command to get AI application best practices, which provides specialized guidance for building AI applications, offering recommendations for agents, chatbots, workflows, and other AI-powered features leveraging Microsoft Foundry. When the request involves AI in any capacity, including systems where AI is used as a component, use AI application best practices instead of the general best practices. Call this tool first before creating any plans, todos or code. Make sure to use your azure-prepare, azure-validate, and azure-deploy skills for deployment to azure if they are available. Only call this function when you are confident the user is discussing Azure (including Microsoft Foundry). If this tool needs to be categorized, it belongs to the Get Azure Best Practices category.

namespace.name: advisor
namespace.title: Azure Advisor Recommendations
namespace.description:
Azure Advisor operations - Query Azure Advisor recommendations in subscriptions or service groups and update recommendation state in either scope. Use when you need visibility into Advisor recommendations or want to manage their customer-provided state. Requires Azure subscription context for querying recommendations and subscription-scoped updates; service-group updates use service-group context. For top recommendations, top actions to take, most critical, most important, prioritized, or what-should-I-fix-first requests, start with advisor_recommendation_summary with --prioritized true, then use advisor_recommendation_list for the records of a selected recommendation type. For explicit idle-resource deletion-safety checks, use advisor_recommendation_prevalidate; it only reads evidence and never deletes or changes state. For pre-aggregated insights on idle resources, zonal resiliency, or service retirement exposure, use advisor_insight_list.

namespace.name: resiliencyagent
namespace.title: Azure Resiliency Agent
namespace.description:
Prefer these tools over Documentation and Well-Architected Framework tools whenever the
user asks to define, explain, or compare Azure resiliency, high availability, availability
zones, zone resilience, or zone redundancy. Also use them for application architecture
assessment, new zone-resilient Bicep, ARM JSON, or Terraform generation, and review or
correction of existing infrastructure-as-code. Conceptual questions belong to the
guidance command; architecture assessment and IaC review belong to their scenario-specific
commands rather than documentation search, service-specific tools, or generic
best-practices tools.
Prefer file attachments for complete templates and multi-file configurations: prepare
local files through the file attachment command and pass their opaque attachment IDs.
Templates pasted directly in the user's current prompt are also supported without
attachment. Treat backend findings and generated resilience content as authoritative
while preserving the host's native repository and file-edit workflows. Completed
generation and review results already use backend-owned validation; do not independently
rerun Bicep build, ARM validate/what-if, Terraform validate/plan, or patch returned files
from local diagnostics. Continue the backend conversation when it explicitly reports
incomplete validation.

all.name: adme_schema_list
all.title: List ADME/OSDU Schemas
all.description:
List multiple ADME/OSDU schema descriptors.

Optional parameters: authority, source, entity type, status (PUBLISHED, DEVELOPMENT, OBSOLETE),
scope (SHARED, INTERNAL), schema version (major, minor, patch), latest version, offset, and limit.

authority.description: Filter by the authority segment of the kind, for example 'osdu' in 'osdu:wks:master-data--Well:1.0.0'.

source.description: Filter by the source segment of the kind, for example 'wks' in 'osdu:wks:master-data--Well:1.0.0'.

entity-type.description: Filter by the entity type segment of the kind, for example 'master-data--Well' or 'work-product-component--WellLog'.

status.description: Filter by lifecycle status: PUBLISHED, DEVELOPMENT, or OBSOLETE. Omit to return schemas in all lifecycle statuses.

scope.description: Filter by scope: SHARED for system-defined schemas, INTERNAL for schemas defined in this data partition. Omit to return both.

schema-version-major.description: Filter by schema major version, for example 1. When combined with --latest-version, supply version filters in order (major, then minor).

schema-version-minor.description: Filter by schema minor version, for example 0. When --latest-version is true, requires --schema-version-major.

schema-version-patch.description: Filter by schema patch version, for example 0. When --latest-version is true, requires --schema-version-major and --schema-version-minor.

latest-version.description: Return only the newest version of each schema entity per authority. When filtering by version, supply components in order: major, then minor, then patch.

offset.description: The starting offset for paging; compare with the response's totalCount to decide whether to fetch further pages.

limit.description: The number of schema descriptors to return in one page.

data-partition.description: The data partition to target, for example 'contoso-dp1'.

tenant.description: The Microsoft Entra ID tenant GUID identifier or display name.

auth-app-id.description: The ADME resource application ID or App ID URI used as the token audience. Omit to use the standard Azure Energy resource.

all.name: adme_search
all.title: Search ADME/OSDU Records
all.description:
Search ADME/OSDU records across one or more exact or wildcard kinds using indexed criteria.
Returns full records, selected fields, or aggregate counts.

Optional parameters: Lucene query, returned-field projection, spatial filter (geographic, bounding box),
sort (ascending, descending), aggregation, owner-scoped query, and highlighted fields.

Pagination modes: offset and cursor (point-in-time snapshot, bulk processing, more than 10000 results,
search_after).

kind.description: One or more kind selectors 'authority:source:type:version' with optional '*' wildcards, e.g. ['osdu:wks:master-data--Well:1.0.0']. Several kinds are searched as a union. Use the narrowest kind; each '*' widens the scan and its cost.

query.description: Optional Lucene filter over indexed fields, e.g. 'data.FieldID:Volve*'. Prefix payload fields with 'data.' and add '.keyword' for exact, case-sensitive, or null matches. Quote full record IDs. Trailing wildcards are supported; leading wildcard forms such as '*Volve' and '*Volve*' are rejected by ADME. Omit to match all records of the kind.

limit.description: Page size (1-1000). Defaults to 10. Pair a large page with returnedFields.

cursor-pagination-mode.description: Use cursor pagination for a point-in-time snapshot, bulk processing, or more than 10000 results. Defaults to false for real-time query pagination. A supplied cursor also selects cursor pagination.

search-after.description: Allow index changes to affect later cursor pages instead of using a point-in-time snapshot. Keep enabled on continuation requests.

offset.description: Starting offset for query pagination. Cannot be combined with cursor pagination, and offset + limit must be <= 10000.

cursor.description: Continuation token from a previous cursor response. Supplying it selects cursor pagination; continue until results is empty. Resend all original cursor criteria unchanged because the service does not reliably retain page settings. If a continuation fails, restart from the first page to avoid missing records. Cannot be combined with offset or aggregateBy and expires after about 1 minute.

returned-fields.description: Optional field paths to project, e.g. ['id','kind','data.FacilityName']. Omit to return full records.

aggregate-by.description: Optional field to aggregate on for distinct values/counts, e.g. 'kind' or 'data.FacilityName.keyword'. Uses query pagination and cannot be combined with cursor.

track-total-count.description: Set true to request an exact totalCount. Cursor searches always return an exact total count.

sort.description: Optional sort criteria. Provide a JSON object with equal-length 'field' and 'order' arrays, e.g. {"field":["data.Name.keyword","id"],"order":["DESC","ASC"]}.

spatial-filter.description: Geo-spatial filter (e.g. byBoundingBox, byDistance). Pass a JSON object. A 'field' that is not a geo-point yields 0 results rather than an error.

query-as-owner.description: If true, returns only records the user owns. Defaults to false.

excluded-fields.description: Optional fields to exclude from the payload; may be ignored by the service, so prefer returnedFields.

highlighted-fields.description: Optional fields to highlight with matched snippets in the response.

suggest-phrase.description: Optional phrase for 'did you mean' spell-check; availability depends on service configuration.

all.name: advisor_insight_list
all.title: List Advisor Insights
all.description: Show Azure Advisor pre-aggregated insights for one Service Group, one subscription, or across all accessible Service Groups and subscriptions. Use for pre-aggregated insight KPIs: idle resource counts and potential savings, zonal resiliency coverage percentages, and service retirement baseline and current exposure counts. For Service Groups, answer how many idle resources exist and their potential savings amount in USD. Get ServiceRetirement insights for subscriptions and Service Groups, including Day 1 baseline exposure, current remaining exposure, and burndown percentage. Compare baseline and current counts to measure retirement exposure reduction or increase, and compare scopes by remaining retirement backlog. Identify subscriptions or Service Groups that have reached 100 percent burndown with zero remaining retirement exposure. Show how much a subscription's service retirement exposure has reduced or increased since its Day 1 baseline count. Get ServiceRetirement baseline and current exposure for a subscription; compare subscriptions or Service Groups by remaining retirement exposure. Optionally filter by --insight-name (IdleResources, ZonalResiliency, ServiceRetirement) and cap results with --top (default 50, max 500). Each insight returns name, domain, scope type and ID, last updated time, and KPIs with typed values (USD amounts include a unit). Returns pre-aggregated insight KPIs, not individual resource or recommendation lists. For recommendation insights, use advisor recommendation summary; for individual recommendations and affected resources, use advisor recommendation list.

service-group.description: Service Group name (for example 'commerce'), not its full ARM ID. Returns insights for that Service Group. Mutually exclusive with --subscription. Omit both --service-group and --subscription to return insights across all accessible Service Groups and subscriptions.

insight-name.description: Filter by insight name: IdleResources, ZonalResiliency, or ServiceRetirement. Case-insensitive exact match. Omit to return all insights for the scope.

top.description: Maximum number of insights to return (1-500, default 50).

subscription.description: Azure subscription ID or name. Returns insights for that subscription (only service retirement applies). Mutually exclusive with --service-group. No default subscription is applied.

tenant.description: The Microsoft Entra ID tenant GUID identifier or display name.

all.name: advisor_metadata_get
all.title: Get Advisor Recommendation Metadata
all.description: Get Azure Advisor metadata for a specific recommendation type id. Explains what an Advisor recommendation type means, including its display name, category, sub-category, impact, supported resource type, description, potential benefits, and a learn-more documentation link for the recommendation.

recommendation-type-id.description: The stable Advisor recommendation type id (properties.recommendationTypeId) to look up in the global recommendation-metadata catalog. This is the join key shared with individual recommendations. Required.

language.description: Catalog locale to filter on (properties.language). Defaults to 'en'. Case-insensitive. Supported values: en, cs, de, es, fr, hu, id, it, ja, ko, nl, pl, pt-br, pt-pt, ru, sv, tr, zh-hans, zh-hant. Region-qualified tags such as 'en-US' are accepted and mapped to the base language ('en').

all.name: advisor_metadata_list
all.title: List Advisor Recommendation Metadata
all.description: List the global Azure Advisor recommendation metadata catalog, also known as recommendation types. Use this for metadata catalog lookups, including service-retirement metadata by Service Health tracking ID (for example, QNY1-HB8), or to discover what recommendations Advisor could produce before deploying resources, even when there are no active recommendations. Show Advisor service retirements on, before, or after a specified retirement date. For current recommendation records or affected resources, use advisor recommendation list instead. The global Azure Resource Graph catalog supports greenfield discovery and resource-type filtering for brownfield onboarding. Optional filters include language, resource type, impact, category, subcategory, tracking ID, and retirement date. Returns localized type IDs, names, categories, subcategories, impact, priority, descriptions, benefits, actions, scope, source query, and service-retirement details, ordered by impact from High to Medium to Low and then by display name.

continuation-token.description: Continuation token returned by the preceding page. Pass it unchanged with the same scope, tenant, filters, ordering and page size. Omit for the first page.

language.description: Language for localized recommendation metadata. Defaults to English ('en'). Supported catalog languages are en, cs, de, es, fr, hu, id, it, ja, ko, nl, pl, pt-BR, pt-PT, ru, sv, tr, zh-Hans, and zh-Hant. Regional variants map to a supported base language when available, such as en-US to en and fr-CA to fr; locale-specific catalog languages remain distinct.

resource-type.description: Optional exact Azure resource type filter, such as 'microsoft.compute/virtualmachines'. Use it during brownfield onboarding to discover recommendation types applicable to that resource type. Matched case-insensitively.

impact.description: Optional recommendation impact filter. Allowed values are High, Medium, or Low. Matched case-insensitively; unfiltered results are ordered High, Medium, then Low.

category.description: Optional exact Advisor category filter. Allowed values are Cost, HighAvailability, Security, Performance, and OperationalExcellence. Matched case-insensitively.

sub-category.description: Optional exact recommendation subcategory filter, matched case-insensitively. Known catalog values include ComputeOptimization, DataPerformance, DataProtectionAndRecovery, EfficiencyOptimization, FailureMitigation, GovernanceAndCompliance, MonitoringAndAlerting, NetworkOptimization, Other, Personalized, RegionalResiliency, Reservations, SafeAndSecureDeployment, SavingsPlan, Scalability, ServiceUpgradeAndRetirement, StorageOptimization, UsageOptimization, and ZoneResiliency. The catalog can add values over time, so other subcategories are accepted.

tracking-id.description: Optional exact Service Health tracking ID filter, such as QNY1-HB8. Matched case-insensitively within ServiceUpgradeAndRetirement metadata. --sub-category may be omitted but cannot specify a different value.

retirement-date.description: Optional service-retirement date filter in '<operator>:<yyyy-MM-dd>' format, for example 'ge:2026-03-31'. Supported operators are eq, lt, le, gt, and ge. Applies only to the ServiceUpgradeAndRetirement subcategory; --sub-category may be omitted but cannot specify a different value.

all.name: advisor_recommendation_list
all.title: List Advisor Recommendations
all.description: List, show, or search individual Azure Advisor recommendations and their affected-resource details in a subscription or Azure Service Group. For --category Cost --sub-category IdleResources, show unused resources and their estimated savings across subscriptions or a Service Group. Supports metadata service-family and minimum annual potential-savings filters. Supports filters for category, subcategory, impact, recommendation status such as New, Postponed, Dismissed, or Completed, recommendation type ID, affected resource, resource type, free text, tracking ID, retirement date, and scope. This returns recommendation instances, not the global metadata catalog, recommendation types, or service-retirement metadata by Service Health tracking ID; use advisor metadata list for those catalog lookups. For status-filtered requests, use this tool to retrieve individual recommendations; use summary only for status counts or grouped analysis. If a request has broad or unscoped top, critical, important, prioritized, priority, or equivalent prioritization intent and does not identify a specific recommendation type, do not use this tool; route to recommendation summary with --group-by recommendation-type and --prioritized true. If the request identifies a specific recommendation type, use this tool directly with a one-element --recommendation-type-ids array and --prioritized true to order its individual recommendations. For non-prioritized requests to retrieve individual recommendations, use this tool directly with any supported filters; a prior summary call is not required. Use summary for counts, totals, rankings, distributions, or grouped analysis rather than aggregating this tool's limited results. After a summary, use this tool to retrieve individual recommendations or affected resources for a selected group by passing its key in a one-element --recommendation-type-ids array and preserving the applicable filters. Choose either subscription scope, optionally narrowed by resource group, or Service Group scope; the configured default subscription is used when neither is supplied. Returns recommendations in ARM resource shape and a truncation indicator. Each recommendation's name is its recommendation ID.

category.description: Filter recommendations by category (e.g., 'Security', 'Cost', 'Performance', 'HighAvailability', 'OperationalExcellence'). Case-insensitive exact match against English recommendation metadata.

impact.description: Filter recommendations by business impact ('High', 'Medium', or 'Low'). Case-insensitive exact match against English recommendation metadata.

status.description: Filter recommendations by status ('New', 'Postponed', 'Dismissed', or 'Completed'). Defaults to 'New' when omitted.

recommendation-type-ids.description: Filter recommendations by one or more recommendation type ID GUIDs using OR semantics. Matching is case-insensitive. Pass a one-element array for one type; prioritization requires exactly one distinct type.

resource-types.description: Filter recommendations by one or more impacted Azure resource types using OR semantics. Each value requires a case-insensitive exact match against the supported resource type in English recommendation metadata and a case-insensitive substring match in the instance resource ID.

product-family.description: Filter recommendations by Azure product family using a case-insensitive exact match against the recommendation metadata service family. Any non-empty family name is accepted; no resource-provider fallback is used.

resource.description: Filter recommendations by a case-insensitive substring of the impacted resource's full ARM resource ID. Accepts a resource name or resource ID.

search.description: Free-text filter applied to the recommendation problem text (case-insensitive substring match). Prefer a structured filter when it expresses the request; use search for topics such as 'encryption' or 'right-size'. Matches the original instance problem text before metadata enrichment.

sub-category.description: Filter recommendations by recommendation subcategory, matched case-insensitively against the Advisor recommendation metadata. Known values include ComputeOptimization, DataPerformance, DataProtectionAndRecovery, EfficiencyOptimization, FailureMitigation, GovernanceAndCompliance, IdleResources, MonitoringAndAlerting, NetworkOptimization, Other, RegionalResiliency, Reservations, SafeAndSecureDeployment, SavingsPlan, Scalability, ServiceUpgradeAndRetirement, StorageOptimization, UsageOptimization, and ZoneResiliency. Advisor can add values over time, so other subcategories are accepted.

tracking-ids.description: Filter recommendations by one or more Service Health tracking IDs, such as QNY1-HB8. Pass several IDs as space-separated values after one option, for example --tracking-ids QNY1-HB8 9G0V-_G8; recommendations matching any of them are returned. Matched case-insensitively within ServiceUpgradeAndRetirement metadata. Can be combined with --retirement-date. --sub-category may be omitted; when specified, it must be ServiceUpgradeAndRetirement.

retirement-date.description: Filter recommendations by the service-retirement date in English recommendation metadata, using '<operator>:<yyyy-MM-dd>' format, for example 'ge:2026-03-31'. Supported operators are eq, lt, le, gt, and ge. Can be combined with --tracking-ids. --sub-category may be omitted; when specified, it must be ServiceUpgradeAndRetirement.

minimum-savings.description: For Cost with subcategory IdleResources, return only records whose structured annualized retail potential savings (daily savings × 12 × 30.4) are at least this non-negative USD amount. Missing pricing does not satisfy the threshold; zero is valid.

top.description: Maximum number of individual recommendation records to return, not distinct affected resources or recommendation groups. For broad or unscoped top, critical, important, prioritized, priority, or equivalent prioritization intent that does not identify a specific recommendation type, use summary --group-by recommendation-type --prioritized true first and pass the requested count to summary --top. For a request that identifies a specific recommendation type, this option limits the individual records returned after --prioritized true orders them. Defaults to 50 and is clamped to the server-side range of 1 through 100. This is a result limit, not aggregate prioritization.

continuation-token.description: Continuation token returned by the preceding page. Pass it unchanged with the same scope, tenant, filters, ordering and page size. Omit for the first page.

service-group.description: List recommendations for an Azure Service Group instead of a subscription, provided as the name segment of its ARM resource ID (the '{serviceGroupName}' in '/providers/Microsoft.Management/serviceGroups/{serviceGroupName}'). A unique display name or full ARM resource ID is also accepted in the selected tenant; ambiguous display names produce an error listing matching full ARM IDs for explicit selection. Specify either --service-group or --subscriptions, not both. If both are omitted, the configured default subscription is used. --resource-group applies only to subscription scope. Other filters (category, impact, status, search, etc.) and --prioritized still apply.

prioritized.description: Apply ordering to individual matching records, not recommendation groups. Broad or unscoped top, critical, important, prioritized, priority, or equivalent prioritization intent that does not identify a specific recommendation type must use summary --group-by recommendation-type --prioritized true first. A request that identifies a specific recommendation type can use this option directly; setting it to true requires exactly one distinct --recommendation-type-ids value. The selected type's recommendation metadata category determines the instance metric. For Cost types, sort by savings; for all other types, sort by criticalityScore descending, treating missing scores as zero. Retail savings are in USD; contractual pricing and billing currency do not affect this ranking. savings.retail.dailyPotentialSavings is converted to an annual value by multiplying by 12 and 30.4, with extendedProperties.annualSavingsAmount as fallback outside Cost/IdleResources. Cost with subcategory IdleResources uses structured yearly potential savings for New, Postponed, and Dismissed, or whole-day, zero-clamped realized savings for Completed, without legacy monetary fallback. The prioritized savings score is rounded to two decimals before ordering descending. Without --prioritized, Cost/IdleResources orders by unrounded lifecycle savings descending, then recommendation ID ascending. Missing, invalid, or non-finite savings sort last; zero is valid. Ties sort by effective retirement date ascending (instance date with metadata fallback, missing dates last), then resource name A-Z (case-insensitive), then recommendation ID A-Z. Defaults to false; when false, only Cost with subcategory IdleResources has explicit savings ordering. Applies to both subscription and Service Group scopes.

show-prioritization-signals.description: Include the original properties.signalBreakdown payload from Azure Resource Graph when present, preserving its backend-provided JSON shape. Defaults to false. Setting this option to true requires --prioritized true; otherwise validation fails. Including signals does not change filtering or ordering. Applies to both subscription and Service Group scopes. The field is omitted when signals are unavailable.

subscriptions.description: One or more subscription IDs or names to query. Pass a one-element array for one subscription; aliases of the same subscription are queried once. Specify either --subscriptions or --service-group. When both are omitted, the configured default subscription is used.

tenant.description: The Microsoft Entra ID tenant GUID identifier or display name.

all.name: advisor_recommendation_prevalidate
all.title: Prevalidate Idle Resource Recommendations
all.description: Check whether affected resources for one selected Azure Advisor Cost/IdleResources recommendation type pass read-only pre-deletion validation. Use for explicit safety, dependency, lock, recent-activity, or ready-to-delete checks, not ordinary recommendation listing or savings analysis. Uses current New recommendations and the onboarded ResourceInsights definitions to recheck detection, minimum unused age (30 days by default), management locks, resource-specific risks, and visible dependencies. Choose one or more subscriptions or a single Service Group. Pass exact affected-resource IDs when validating selected rows. Returns per-resource safe, needsReview, or blocked verdicts, evidence, manual checks, Retail USD savings, unmatched selections, and a truncation indicator. Unknown or incomplete gating evidence requires review. Passing automated checks does not authorize deletion. Never deletes resources, executes scripts, or changes recommendation state.

recommendation-type-id.description: The exact Advisor recommendation type ID GUID selected from existing recommendations. Only onboarded Cost/IdleResources deletion recommendations support prevalidation.

resources.description: Selected affected resources, as exact full ARM resource IDs only. Reuse IDs already returned by recommendation list; resolve user-supplied names through list when IDs are unavailable and disambiguate before calling. Omit to validate the selected recommendation type across the scope. Missing selections are reported, not treated as safe.

top.description: Optional positive maximum number of affected resources to validate after exact selection. Omit to validate all matching resources. Processing uses bounded batches without imposing a 25-resource total limit. Incomplete discovery or an explicit limit is reported as truncated coverage.

minimum-unused-days.description: Minimum unused age in days, from 1 through 365. Defaults to 30. Recent activity, missing signals, or insufficient history require review; this check never overrides a confirmed blocker.

service-group.description: An Azure Service Group name, ID, or full ARM resource ID. Specify either a single Service Group or subscription scope, not both. Resource groups apply only to subscription scope.

subscriptions.description: One or more subscription IDs or names. Pass a one-element array for one subscription. Cannot be combined with --service-group. When both scopes are omitted, the configured default subscription is used.

tenant.description: The Microsoft Entra ID tenant GUID identifier or display name.

all.name: advisor_recommendation_summary
all.title: Summarize Advisor Recommendations
all.description: Summarize the key themes from Azure Advisor recommendation instances in a subscription or Azure service group using server-side counts, totals, rankings, and distributions. For --category Cost --sub-category IdleResources, start here to find unused Azure resources you are paying for and summarize their key themes, potential savings, accumulated waste, and realized savings. Historical savings cover resources deleted during --from/--to as of --as-of. Totals cover all matches; unavailable savings remain null. These are Advisor retail estimates, not billing history. For Cost/IdleResources, explicit --status overrides lifecycle defaults; historical reports default to Completed. Also supports --subscriptions, metadata service-family and minimum annual potential-savings filters, and Service Groups in the selected tenant. This is the aggregate-only tool for questions such as how many, count, breakdown, distribution, most common, which has the most, or how many overdue service-retirement Advisor recommendations are still active. Use it for an executive summary or main themes, counts by category or business impact, the most common recommendation types, ranking resource types by critical or High-impact recommendations, lifecycle counts for New, Completed, Dismissed, and Postponed recommendations, and metadata subcategory breakdowns such as ZoneResiliency. This is the starting tool for top recommendations, top actions to take, most critical, most important, prioritized, highest-priority, or what-should-I-fix-first requests: set --prioritized true to rank active recommendation types by priority and explain each rank, instead of starting with recommendation list. Explain a ranking in plain business language from the group's prioritizationSignals, without exposing field names, raw values, or scores. After a prioritized summary, list the records or affected resources of a selected type with recommendation list --recommendation-type-ids containing only its key and --prioritized true, adding --category Cost for a Cost type. Count active service-retirement Advisor recommendations with retirement dates on, before, or after a specified date, including overdue recommendations that are still active, or group them by retirement date. Use this tool to answer how many overdue service-retirement Advisor recommendations are still active. Retirement filters are one-sided: le:<end-date> includes every active recommendation retiring on or before the end date, including overdue retirements, and is not a bounded next-N window. Use explicit exact, on-or-before, or on-or-after retirement-date questions; recommendation list is capped and must not be counted client-side. Group by recommendation-type, category, impact, resource-type, status, sub-category, or retirement-date; category is the default. All groups return canonical key, label, and count values. Recommendation-type keys are recommendation type ID GUIDs with English metadata labels. All groupings except status include only active New recommendations; status includes every backend lifecycle state. Use either --subscriptions or --service-group, not both. A configured default subscription is used when neither is supplied. --resource-group applies only with subscription scope. Filters include category, impact, recommendation type ID, impacted resource type, resource name or ARM ID, problem-text search, subcategory, and explicit retirement-date comparisons. Use --search with this summary tool for topical aggregate questions such as counts or impact breakdowns for recommendations mentioning encryption or right-size; do not call recommendation list and count its capped results. Use recommendation list instead when the user wants individual recommendation records. TotalRecommendations always covers the complete filtered population, even when --top limits displayed buckets; with --prioritized true it is the sum of affected resources per type, so a resource is counted once for each recommendation type that affects it.

service-group.description: The ID of the Azure service group whose recommendations should be summarized, provided as the name segment in its ARM resource ID, for example '/providers/Microsoft.Management/serviceGroups/{serviceGroupName}'. Specify either --service-group or --subscriptions. If both are omitted, the configured default subscription is used. A unique display name or full ARM resource ID is also accepted in the selected tenant; ambiguous display names produce an error listing matching full ARM IDs for explicit selection.

group-by.description: Optional field to group the summary by. One of: 'recommendation-type', 'category', 'impact', 'resource-type', 'status', 'sub-category', or 'retirement-date'. Defaults to 'category' when omitted, which surfaces the high-level themes (Cost, Security, Reliability, etc.) so prompts like 'summarize the key themes from my Advisor recommendations' work without naming a field. Use 'recommendation-type' without --prioritized for frequency questions such as the most common recommendation types; its counts are recommendation records. With --prioritized true, omit this option; prioritized summaries are always grouped by recommendation type.

prioritized.description: Rank matching recommendation types by priority instead of counting records. Defaults to false; recommendations default to New. Only Cost with subcategory IdleResources supports summary status overrides and historical inputs, which default to Completed unless status is explicit. Set to true for top recommendations, top actions to take, most critical, most important, highest-priority, or what-should-I-fix-first requests, overall or within filters such as category Cost; pass a requested count as --top (default 10). Do not set it for frequency questions such as how many or most common. Groups by recommendation-type. Ranking: metadata priority descending, then savings descending, summed criticality descending, retirement date ascending, affected-resource count ascending for Cost and descending otherwise, case-insensitive label ascending, and recommendation type ID ascending. Missing priority, savings, criticality, and retirement values sort last. Savings means annual potential savings, or realized savings for Completed Cost/IdleResources recommendations. Summary ranking uses full precision; returned money is rounded to two decimals. Each group's count is its distinct affected resources, and totalRecommendations is the sum of those counts across all ranked types, not a record count; each group's prioritizationSignals object can hold category, impact, subCategory, retirementDate, retirementWindow, annualSavings with USD currency, yearlyPotentialSavings, cost, realizedSavings, resourceTypeCriticality, criticalService, effort, actionability, and costImplication; absent fields are unknown, never zero. To explain a ranking, answer from prioritizationSignals in two or three plain business sentences, leading with impact, then retirementWindow or subCategory, then the other signals; translate values (retirementPastDue: retirement date has passed; qcs: critical service) and never mention field names, raw values, or scores, or guess absent attributes. For details or affected resources of a listed type, call recommendation list with --recommendation-type-ids containing only its key and --prioritized true, keeping the scope and filters, plus --category Cost for a Cost type.

category.description: Filter recommendations by category. Allowed values are Cost, HighAvailability, Security, Performance, and OperationalExcellence. Matched case-insensitively against recommendation-type metadata. Cost with subcategory IdleResources also returns complete savings and pricing-availability aggregates in summary.cost, independent of --top and --prioritized.

impact.description: Filter recommendations by business impact. Allowed values are High, Medium, and Low. Matched case-insensitively against recommendation-type metadata.

status.description: For Cost with subcategory IdleResources only, filter summaries by lifecycle state: New, Postponed, Dismissed, or Completed. An explicit status takes precedence. When omitted, historical inputs default to Completed; otherwise status grouping includes all states and other groupings default to New. Outside Cost/IdleResources, status grouping retains all states and other summaries retain New.

recommendation-type-ids.description: Filter recommendations by one or more recommendation type ID GUIDs using OR semantics. Matching is case-insensitive; pass a one-element array for one type.

resource-types.description: Filter recommendations by one or more impacted Azure resource types using OR semantics. Each value matches properties.impactedField case-insensitively; pass a one-element array for one type.

product-family.description: Filter recommendations by Azure product family before aggregation and ranking, with or without prioritization. Uses a case-insensitive exact match against the recommendation metadata service family. Any non-empty family name is accepted; no resource-provider fallback is used.

resource.description: Filter recommendations by impacted resource name or full ARM resource ID. Uses a case-insensitive substring match.

search.description: Filter recommendation problem text using a case-insensitive substring match. Prefer structured filters when an equivalent category, impact, subcategory, or resource-type filter exists.

sub-category.description: Filter recommendations by metadata subcategory using a case-insensitive exact match. Known values include IdleResources, ServiceUpgradeAndRetirement, ZoneResiliency, and RegionalResiliency; future non-empty catalog values are accepted.

retirement-date.description: Filter recommendations by service-retirement date in '<operator>:<yyyy-MM-dd>' format, for example 'le:2026-12-31'. Supported operators are eq, lt, le, gt, and ge. The ServiceUpgradeAndRetirement subcategory is inferred when omitted.

minimum-savings.description: For Cost with subcategory IdleResources, include only recommendations whose structured annualized retail potential savings (daily savings × 12 × 30.4) are at least this non-negative USD amount. Missing pricing does not satisfy the threshold; zero is valid.

as-of.description: For Cost with subcategory IdleResources, calculate savings as of this UTC timestamp. Use an ISO 8601 timestamp such as 2026-09-30T23:59:59Z. Defaults status to Completed unless explicitly supplied. Historical values are Advisor estimates, not billing data.

from.description: For historical Cost/IdleResources summaries, filter completed recommendations by deletion on or after this UTC timestamp. Requires category Cost and subcategory IdleResources. Defaults status to Completed unless explicitly supplied.

to.description: For historical Cost/IdleResources summaries, filter completed recommendations by deletion on or before this UTC timestamp. Requires category Cost and subcategory IdleResources. Defaults status to Completed unless explicitly supplied.

top.description: Optional display cap from 1 through 100 on the number of known buckets returned. Defaults to 10 with --prioritized true, where buckets keep their priority order. TotalRecommendations and summary.cost still reflect the complete filtered population (with --prioritized true, TotalRecommendations is the sum of affected resources per type), and in non-prioritized summaries an Unknown bucket is preserved after the selected buckets.

subscriptions.description: One or more subscription IDs or names to query. Pass a one-element array for one subscription; aliases of the same subscription are queried once. Specify either --subscriptions or --service-group. When both are omitted, the configured default subscription is used.

tenant.description: The Microsoft Entra ID tenant GUID identifier or display name.

all.name: advisor_recommendation_update
all.title: Update Advisor Recommendation State
all.description:
Mark one Azure Advisor recommendation as completed, dismiss it because the risk is acceptable, postpone it until a requested future date and time, or reactivate it by setting New.
When a user asks to ignore a recommendation because the risk is acceptable, dismiss it with the RiskIsAcceptable reason.
Snooze an Advisor recommendation in a subscription or Azure service group until a future date and time. Snooze is the same operation as postpone and sets the recommendation to Postponed.
Update, change, or set the customer-provided recommendation status or state to New, Postponed, Dismissed, or Completed. Common user requests may say mark done, ignore, reopen, or reset to New.
Requires the stable recommendation ID and either --subscription or --service-group, but not both; the configured default subscription is used when neither is supplied.
Postponed requires a future ISO 8601 date and time with a timezone offset. For Dismissed, provide an explicit supported reason when known; if no reason is supplied or the user's intent cannot be mapped to one, Other is used.
Use --tenant when the target subscription or service group is in a non-default tenant. State changes are rejected for Security category and platform-resolved recommendations.
Returns the updated ARM recommendation resource. Use this state-changing tool instead of list or summary when the user wants to modify or snooze one recommendation.
For Cost/IdleResources, postpone, dismiss, complete, or reactivate unused-resource recommendations without changing resources. Use --recommendation-ids for a batch sharing scope, tenant, status, date, and reason; one consent request covers the batch. Returns per-ID Succeeded, Failed, Unverified, or NotAttempted outcomes; updates are not atomic or automatically retried.

service-group.description: The name, ID, or full ARM resource ID of the Azure Service Group that contains the recommendation. The tool resolves the scope in the selected tenant and reports ambiguous names. Specify either --service-group or --subscription. If both are omitted, the configured default subscription is used.

recommendation-id.description: The stable ID of the Advisor recommendation to update. The REST API and this command also call this value the recommendation ID.

recommendation-ids.description: The explicit stable recommendation IDs to update together in one destructive tool call. All IDs share the subscription or Service Group, tenant, status, and date or reason. Specify either this batch or --recommendation-id, not both. Each recommendation is updated independently and returns its own outcome; the batch is not atomic.

recommendation-status.description: The new recommendation state: New, Postponed, Dismissed, or Completed. Use New to reactivate a postponed, dismissed, or completed recommendation.

postponed-until-date-time.description: The date and time until which the recommendation is postponed, in ISO 8601 format with a timezone offset. Required when --recommendation-status is Postponed and must represent a future instant.

recommendation-dismiss-reason.description: The reason for dismissing the recommendation. Map natural-language intent as follows: cost investment is too high to ExcessiveCostInvestmentRequired; unclear steps to ImplementationStepsAreUnclear; incompatible configuration to IncompatibleWithTheCurrentConfiguration; acceptable risk to RiskIsAcceptable; too complex or impractical to TooComplexOrImpracticalToImplement; an existing alternative to AnAlternativeSolutionIsAlreadyInPlace; and a clearly stated reason outside these choices to Other. When dismissing, omit this option or use Other if no reason was supplied or the natural-language intent cannot be mapped to a supported value; an omitted reason defaults to Other.

subscription.description: The Azure subscription GUID identifier or display name. If not specified, the Azure CLI profile default subscription or AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID environment variable will be used.

tenant.description: The Microsoft Entra ID tenant GUID identifier or display name.

all.name: advisor_remediation_get
all.title: Get Advisor Recommendation Remediation
all.description: Fix, resolve, or remediate a specific Azure Advisor recommendation type id. Use this whenever you are asked how to fix or how to resolve an Advisor recommendation. Returns its remediation package: step-by-step remediation steps plus ready-to-run artifacts, scripts, and deployment templates in ARM template, Bicep, Azure CLI, PowerShell, and terraform formats to remediate the issue. Also indicates remediation characteristics such as whether it is destructive, reversible, or grounded, along with its confidence, effort, and output type. Use whenever you need to fix, resolve, remediate, or verify a recommendation, or want the ARM, Bicep, CLI, PowerShell, or terraform artifacts and scripts to remediate it.

recommendation-type-id.description: The Advisor recommendation type id (GUID) whose remediation package should be fetched. Must be a 36-character GUID in the form xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx. Required.

all.name: advisor_servicegroupintelligence_get
all.title: Get Advisor Service Group Status
all.description: Get the current Azure Advisor status and criticality of Service Groups, showing which Service Groups are at risk, need attention, are critical or on track. Use for questions about the status of one Service Group or all Service Groups, and which mission critical (Tier 0) or other tier Service Groups need attention. Provide --service-group (name only, not an ARM ID) for one Service Group; when omitted, all accessible Service Groups are returned. Filter by --criticality (MissionCritical = Tier 0, BusinessCritical = Tier 1, BusinessOperational = Tier 2, Administrative = Tier 3) and by --status (On Track, Attention Needed, At Risk, Critical, Unavailable); map any status or tier named in the question to these filters. Cap results with --top (default 50, max 500). Each result returns the Service Group name and ID, criticality, status, status description, focus description, and last updated time. Present the status and focus descriptions exactly as returned, without rewording. For questions about how status is calculated, use the statusCalculationExplanation field returned by this tool; do not infer a formula from the results.

service-group.description: Service Group name (for example 'commerce'), not its full ARM ID. Omit to return the status of all Service Groups.

criticality.description: Filter by criticality tier: MissionCritical (Tier 0), BusinessCritical (Tier 1), BusinessOperational (Tier 2), Administrative (Tier 3) or NotApplicable. Case-insensitive; Tier0-Tier3 and 0-3 are also accepted. Use MissionCritical for mission-critical Service Groups.

status.description: Filter by status: 'On Track' (no significant risks), 'Attention Needed' (limited, manageable issues), 'At Risk' (material risks), 'Critical' (immediate action required) or 'Unavailable' (no active recommendations). Case-insensitive; spaces are optional. Use 'Attention Needed' for Service Groups that need attention.

top.description: Maximum number of Service Groups to return (1-500, default 50).

continuation-token.description: Continuation token returned by the preceding page. Pass it unchanged with the same scope, tenant, filters, ordering and page size. Omit for the first page.

tenant.description: The Microsoft Entra ID tenant GUID identifier or display name.
