all.name: amgmcp_cost_analysis
all.title: Get Azure cost analysis
all.description: Show Azure cost analysis. Use groupBy to choose the breakdowns: by service (MeterCategory), region, resource type, and - the one that identifies what to actually downsize or delete - by individual resource. groupBy defaults to 'service,region,resourceType'; pass groupBy='resource' for per-resource costs, or groupBy='resourceGroup' for cost per resource group. groupBy needs a subscriptionId: with none, the tool queries the service breakdown only, whatever groupBy asks for. If no subscription ID is given, only the first few accessible subscriptions are queried and the response says how many exist; list them with amgmcp_query_azure_subscriptions and pass the ones you want. Cost Management rate limits are shared across the whole tenant, so prefer one subscription per call and honor retryAfterSeconds instead of retrying immediately. Stop after three unsuccessful retries and report the rate limit.

subscriptionId.description: Azure subscription ID to query costs for. Accepts several, separated by commas. If omitted, only the first few accessible subscriptions are queried (see the response's accessibleSubscriptions and truncated fields) - a single data source can reach hundreds, and the Cost Management quotas are shared tenant-wide. Omitting it also narrows the response to the 'service' breakdown only, whatever groupBy asks for. Use amgmcp_query_azure_subscriptions to list subscriptions, then name the ones you want.

startTime.description: Start time: RFC3339 (e.g. '2024-01-15T00:00:00Z') or relative expression (e.g. 'now-1h', 'now-7d').

endTime.description: End time: RFC3339 (e.g. '2024-01-16T00:00:00Z') or relative expression (e.g. 'now', 'now-1h').

groupBy.description: Which breakdowns to return: 'service', 'region', 'resourceType', 'resourceGroup', 'resource', or several separated by commas. Defaults to 'service,region,resourceType', and every value here is honored only when subscriptionId names at least one subscription - with subscriptionId omitted only the 'service' breakdown is queried, whatever groupBy or the default asks for, so name a subscription to get the region, resourceType, resourceGroup or resource breakdowns. Add 'resource' for cost per individual resource - the breakdown that identifies what to downsize or delete; it is opt-in because its row count scales with the size of the subscription. Add 'resourceGroup' for cost per resource group - small and single-page. Resources in a group usually share a deployment and lifecycle, so this groups spend by what was deployed together rather than by service category, and several identically-priced resources in one group is often repeated provisioning that was never cleaned up. A value that names no breakdown fails the call with [invalid_argument] and the valid values; nothing is queried.

topResources.description: Maximum number of rows in the per-resource breakdown, highest cost first. Only applies when groupBy includes 'resource'. Any remainder is reported as a single '(other resources)' entry so the list still reconciles to totalCost. Defaults to 40, maximum 200; a larger value is reduced to 200 and a non-positive one replaced by 40, with a warning.

all.name: amgmcp_dashboard_inspect
all.title: Inspect dashboard
all.description: Inspect a dashboard of Azure Monitor dashboards with Grafana, saved or built-in: its panels, their queries, or a JSONPath read of the raw JSON. Get dashboardUid from amgmcp_dashboard_search. The mode comes from which optional arguments you set. Default (no optional args): summary mode: title, slim panel list (panelId, title, type, and path, its JSONPath), panel-type histogram, template variables, time range, tags, metadata and nextSteps recipes. Start here. includeQueries=true (or panelId, or variables): panel_queries mode: per-panel queries (KQL/PromQL/etc.) with datasource uid+type. panelId filters to one panel; variables substitutes template variables the way Grafana 12/13 does: each target's processedQuery replaces its query, plus processedResources (+ processedDatabase for ADX) + requiredVariables. Only Azure Monitor Logs and Azure Data Explorer targets carry a toolCall: call toolCall.tool with toolCall.arguments unchanged. When present, arguments is complete (the resource, or the cluster and database, the time range, and the variables passed or saved); it is withheld while toolCall.missingVariables is not empty (pass them in variables) or the target cannot run as in Grafana, and toolCall.notes say why. The KQL has the panel's window written in as literal times (toolCall.timeRange); edit them for another window. A Logs panel that takes its window from the dashboard gets argumentsWithoutTimeFilter instead: add the time filter toolCall.notes give. Azure Monitor targets carry resources, the ARM resource IDs the query runs against (they appear nowhere in the KQL); built-in dashboards build them from variables such as $sub, $rg and $res (a resource's name, not its ID), so pass those in variables. jsonPath: property mode: a JSONPath read of the raw dashboard JSON, returning value (always an array), empty (true on no match) and the version. jsonPath selects property mode and cannot be combined with includeQueries / panelId / variables (those select panel_queries mode); a conflict is an error, never ignored.

dashboardUid.description: Dashboard uid from amgmcp_dashboard_search: a saved dashboard's (subscriptions~<subscription id>~resourceGroups~<resource group>~providers~Microsoft.Dashboard~dashboards~<name>) or a built-in dashboard's (e.g. GitHubCopilot). A saved dashboard's Azure resource ID also works.

jsonPath.description: Optional JSONPath expression. When set, performs a surgical JSONPath read against the raw dashboard JSON and returns the matched values. Goessner-style; single and double quotes both work, and the leading '$.' is conventional but optional. A panel inside a collapsed row sits in that row's own panels array ($.panels[i].panels[j]), which '$.panels[...]' does not reach; the '..' in the recipes below does, and summary mode gives each panel's exact path. An empty '$.panels[...]' filter or wildcard read returns a hint when '$..panels[...]' would match inside collapsed rows. Recipes: the dashboard title '$.title'; panel titles, rows included '$..panels[*].title'; one panel by id '$..panels[?(@.id==2)]'; every datasource uid its queries use '$..targets[*].datasource.uid'; variable names '$.templating.list[*].name'; query variables '$.templating.list[?(@.type=="query")].name'; text-panel markdown '$..panels[?(@.type=="text")].options.content'. The match cap is 1000 - refine the expression if you hit it. Mutually exclusive with includeQueries / panelId / variables.

includeQueries.description: When true, returns each panel's underlying queries (KQL/PromQL/etc.) with datasource uid+type, plus resources (the ARM resource IDs an Azure Monitor target is scoped to - needed to re-run its KQL through amgmcp_query_resource_log). Combine with panelId to filter to a single panel, or with variables to substitute template variables. Azure Monitor Logs targets carry toolCall, a ready-to-send call of amgmcp_query_resource_log: send toolCall.arguments unchanged, and when arguments is absent read toolCall.notes for why. Its query is plain KQL: the variables substituted, and the data source's macros ($__timeFilter, $__timeFrom, $__timeTo, $__contains, ...) and $__from / $__to written as the panel's window, which toolCall.timeRange gives. A panel set to take its time range from the dashboard, whose query has no time filter of its own, gets toolCall.argumentsWithoutTimeFilter instead of arguments: Grafana sends that window beside the query and amgmcp_query_resource_log sends none, so add the time filter toolCall.notes give before the call. Built-in dashboards do this, and build their resource from variables such as $sub, $rg and $res, which holds the resource's name, not its ID: pass those in variables. A Logs call runs on one resource, so a target that queries several, or names its workspace only by id, gets no arguments. Azure Data Explorer targets carry a toolCall of amgmcp_kusto_query: its query is plain KQL too, with the variables substituted and the macros written as the panel's window, and its clusterUrl comes from the target's clusterUri; a target with no clusterUri fails in Grafana too and gets no arguments. A target with arguments or argumentsWithoutTimeFilter has no query or processedQuery: they hold the query as it runs. arguments is present only when every variable the target uses has a value: while toolCall.missingVariables is not empty it is withheld (a literal $name would be refused by the tool or match nothing), so pass those names in variables. Other targets, such as Prometheus, show their query with no toolCall. Azure Monitor METRICS targets have no query string, so they return a synthesized description instead - 'metric: <namespace>/<name> | aggregation: ... | dimensions: ... | resources: ... | alias: ...' - and TRACES targets return 'traces: <traceTypes> | operationId: ...'. skippedByGrafana marks targets Grafana itself does not run. Mutually exclusive with jsonPath.

panelId.description: Optional panel ID filter. When set, returns just the queries for that single panel (implies includeQueries=true), inside a collapsed row too. An id that is not on the dashboard fails with panel_not_found, listing the panel ids; a row's id fails with panel_is_row, listing the row's panels. Mutually exclusive with jsonPath.

variables.description: Optional template variable values for substitution in panel queries (implies includeQueries=true). When provided, each target's response includes processedQuery (with variables substituted) in place of query (a target whose toolCall has arguments or argumentsWithoutTimeFilter has neither: they hold the query as it runs), processedResources (the Azure resource scope with variables substituted) and requiredVariables fields. Example: {"sub": "<subscription id>", "rg": "<resource group>", "res": "<resource name>"}. Values use the same form summary mode reports as a variable's current value: for a multi-value variable pass the values comma-separated ({"State": "ACTIVE,MITIGATED"}, writing \, for a comma and \\ for a backslash inside a value), and pass "$__all" for All. "$__all" is expanded only when the variable has a custom allValue or known options (custom variables do, unless a JSON-format query does not parse); for a query variable saved without options the reference is left as written, and the variable is named in the response's warnings, so pass its values instead (one value for a single-value variable). Substitution follows Grafana 12/13, so processedQuery is the text Grafana sends: formats such as ${State:singlequote} are applied as written, and a reference without one takes the data source's own default, which depends on the variable. For a multi-value or include-All variable Azure Data Explorer and Azure Monitor quote each value and Prometheus regex-escapes; a plain single-select value is inserted as is (Prometheus escapes only \ and '). A constant variable's own $refs are expanded before it is formatted. ADX $__contains/$__escapeMulti are expanded, except one that uses a dashboard variable or a frontend built-in ($__from, ${__user.login}, ...) that has no value here, directly or through an allValue, a custom option or a constant's text: that one stays unexpanded, with its other references substituted. $__all_variables and $__url_time_range are inserted unformatted, processedDatabase is filled for ADX targets, and Azure Monitor resources expand to one entry per value. Backend macros such as $__timeFilter(col), $__timeFrom or $__rate_interval are left for the data source in processedQuery; an Azure Data Explorer or Azure Monitor Logs toolCall has them expanded. requiredVariables lists the dashboard variables, including those a listed variable's All, options or constant text is computed from, and the built-ins Grafana's frontend fills in ($__from, $__to, $__interval, ...; a built-in read with a path, such as ${__user.login}, is listed and supplied under that whole name, e.g. {"__user.login": "alice"}), not other $words such as KQL $left. On Azure Monitor Logs and Azure Data Explorer targets, toolCall.defaultedVariables, toolCall.missingVariables and toolCall.undefinedVariables say where each value in toolCall.arguments came from, and $__from, $__to and $__timezone are filled from the panel's window and the dashboard's time zone unless you pass them. For an ADX or Logs toolCall, __from and __to (epoch milliseconds) also set the window its time macros are written with, and ADX $__timeInterval needs __interval (e.g. "5m"). A query (or custom, or data source) variable computed from a variable you pass with a value other than the saved one does not keep its saved value, which may belong to the old value: Grafana recomputes it, so it is in toolCall.missingVariables until you pass it too. A name the dashboard does not define is not used (Grafana leaves such references as written) and is named in the response's warnings. Other targets carry no such fields and fill in no saved values: a variable you did not pass stays as written in processedQuery, so compare requiredVariables with the names you passed before running it. Mutually exclusive with jsonPath.

all.name: amgmcp_dashboard_search
all.title: Search dashboards
all.description: Search the dashboards of Azure Monitor dashboards with Grafana: the user's saved dashboards, which are Azure resources found with Azure Resource Graph, then the built-in dashboards. Each hit has uid, title, url (an Azure portal link) and tags. A saved dashboard also has location, subscriptionId and resourceGroup; a built-in one has builtIn, description, section, category and resourceType. A saved dashboard's tags come from Azure, as each Grafana tag Azure holds and then other tags as name:value, so an empty list does not mean the dashboard JSON has no tags. query is a plain text match that ignores case, and a dashboard matches when it holds every word, in any order. On a saved dashboard it reads the name, resource group and Azure tags: panels, panel queries and tags inside the dashboard JSON are not read. A saved dashboard's title in each hit is its Azure resource name: an older dashboard can hold a different title in its JSON, and a search for that title finds nothing. On a built-in dashboard it reads the title, description, tags, section, category, sub-category, resource type and the panels' titles and descriptions, but not panel queries. Few built-in dashboards say AKS, so search for kubernetes or the resource type instead. At most 200 saved dashboards are listed, newest first; truncated is true when more match. This tool does not create dashboards: users create them in the Azure portal.

query.description: The words to find: a dashboard matches when it holds all of them, in any order. Leave it out to list dashboards.

includeProvisioned.description: Include the built-in dashboards in the result. Default: true. Set it to false to list saved dashboards only.

subscriptionIds.description: Limit saved dashboards to these Azure subscription IDs (GUIDs, at most 500): one ID, a list, or IDs separated by commas. Leave it out to search every subscription the user can read. A subscription the user cannot read is skipped with no notice, and the call fails when the user can read none of them. Built-in dashboards belong to no subscription, so this does not limit them.

all.name: amgmcp_dashboard_update
all.title: Update dashboard
all.description: Change a saved dashboard of Azure Monitor dashboards with Grafana. It cannot create a dashboard (users create them in the Azure portal) or change a built-in one. Two modes, selected by which arguments you provide. PATCH MODE (for any change) - provide dashboardUid (from amgmcp_dashboard_search) and operations. Each operation has op and path: "add" or "replace" with value, "remove", or "replace_text" with oldText and newText, which replaces the one occurrence of oldText inside the string at path. Use replace_text to change a few lines of a long query or text panel without re-sending the string; oldText must occur exactly once (else text_not_found or text_not_unique), so include enough nearby text. The operations parameter has examples. Patch paths are a strict JSONPath subset with numeric indices ($.panels[2].targets[0].query); quote a name that is not an identifier: $.options['Needs fix']. Filter expressions ([?(@.id==2)]), wildcards ([*]) and recursive descent (..) are rejected; amgmcp_dashboard_inspect gives each panel's path. Operations apply in order and all or none are saved. Pass version (from amgmcp_dashboard_inspect or this tool's last result) so the patch is refused with version_mismatch if the dashboard was saved after your read. The result's changes says what each operation changed (short values in full, long ones by size and line), so you need not re-read the dashboard to check. validateOnly=true does all of this but saves nothing (status 'validated'). REPLACE MODE - provide dashboard (full JSON object) with the uid and version amgmcp_dashboard_inspect reports, to wholly replace the dashboard; it costs far more context than a patch. overwrite is replace only; without it a wrong version fails with version_mismatch. A save sets the title to the dashboard's Azure resource name (warning title_not_saved), and amgmcp_dashboard_search reads tags from Azure, so changed tags may not show there. This tool may make destructive modifications.

dashboard.description: Full dashboard JSON object. Required for replace mode. Mutually exclusive with dashboardUid + operations. It wholly replaces the dashboard its uid names, and cannot create one: it must hold the uid and version amgmcp_dashboard_inspect reports for a dashboard that exists, and a title.

dashboardUid.description: uid of a saved dashboard to patch, from amgmcp_dashboard_search: subscriptions~<subscription id>~resourceGroups~<resource group>~providers~Microsoft.Dashboard~dashboards~<name>. A saved dashboard's Azure resource ID also works. A built-in dashboard cannot be changed. Required for patch mode. Mutually exclusive with dashboard.

operations.description: Array of patch operations to apply to the dashboard at dashboardUid. Required for patch mode. Each entry has op (one of "add", "replace", "remove", "replace_text") and path (a strict JSONPath subset, numeric indices only); add and replace also take value (the value to insert), and replace_text takes oldText and newText instead of value. replace_text edits part of the string at path: oldText must occur in it exactly once and is replaced by newText (an empty newText deletes it). oldText is matched exactly, case, spaces and line endings included; send real line breaks, not a backslash followed by n. Zero matches fail with text_not_found and several with text_not_unique (with the lines they start on, or the character positions in a one-line string): add nearby lines to oldText until it matches one place. Use it to change a few lines of a long query or text panel without re-sending the whole string, and send several replace_text operations in one call for several edits. Operations apply in order, each to the result of the one before, and all or none are saved: if any fails, nothing is written. Maximum 100 operations per call. Path examples: '$.title' — the dashboard title; '$.panels[0].title' — the first panel's title; '$.panels[2].targets[0].expr' — the first query of the third panel; '$.panels/-' — append a new panel (the /- suffix means "append to array"); '$.panels[2].targets/-' — append a new query target to the third panel; '$.panels[4].panels[1].title' — the second panel inside the collapsed row at $.panels[4]. Quote a property name that is not an identifier (spaces, dots, dashes, a leading digit) with ['...'] or ["..."], as jsonPath reads do, e.g. $.panels[3].fieldConfig.defaults.mappings[0].options['Needs fix'].color; inside the quotes, \\, \' and \" stand for a backslash and the quotes. Filter expressions (e.g. [?(@.id==2)]), wildcards ([*]) and recursive descent (..) are not supported here, nor are JSON Pointer paths such as /panels/0/title; amgmcp_dashboard_inspect's summary gives every panel's exact path, or find the numeric index with a jsonPath read. replace, remove and replace_text need the path to exist; add creates its last segment. Common patterns: rename a panel — {op:"replace", path:"$.panels[0].title", value:"New Title"}; add a panel — {op:"add", path:"$.panels/-", value:{ /* full panel JSON */ }}; remove a panel — {op:"remove", path:"$.panels[2]"}; add a query to a panel — {op:"add", path:"$.panels[1].targets/-", value:{ /* target JSON */ }}; change one line of a query — {op:"replace_text", path:"$.panels[1].targets[0].query", oldText:"| where Level == 'Error'", newText:"| where Level in ('Error', 'Critical')"}.

message.description: Commit message for the dashboard's version history. Recommended for both modes. Write it in ASCII: this server cannot save other characters, so it leaves them out, with the warning message_not_ascii. Cut to 500 bytes.

overwrite.description: Replace mode only. When false (default), a save is refused if the version in dashboard is not the dashboard's current version. When true, the save goes ahead whatever that version is, and replaces any change saved since; the dashboard's earlier versions stay in its history. Setting this in patch mode is rejected; in patch mode pass version instead. Set true cautiously.

version.description: Patch mode only, recommended. The dashboard version your operations were worked out from — every amgmcp_dashboard_inspect mode returns it, and so does this tool's previous result. When set, the patch is applied only if the dashboard is still at that version; if it was saved since, nothing is written and the call fails with version_mismatch, so re-read, recompute the operations (numeric indices such as $.panels[3] may have shifted) and retry. When omitted, the patch is applied to whatever version is current. Rejected in replace mode, where the version field inside dashboard plays this role.

validateOnly.description: When true, does everything a save does except the save: in patch mode it reads the dashboard, checks version, applies the operations and runs content validation, then returns the usual result with status 'validated', the changes the operations would make, the warnings, and version unchanged (the version to pass on the real call). Nothing is written. Use it to check a large or risky patch before saving it. In replace mode it reads the dashboard and validates the JSON; a stale version is found only on a real save.

all.name: amgmcp_health_model_get_history
all.title: Get Azure Monitor health model history
all.description: Read how an entity of an Azure Monitor health model changed over time. Without signalName: the entity's state changes (occurredAt, previousState, newState, reason), newest first. reason ChildEntityTransition means a child entity changed it: follow the relationships of amgmcp_health_model_inspect to the child and read its history; SignalTransition means one of the entity's own signals did. With signalName: that signal's evaluations, merged into runs of one state (startTime, endTime, healthState, points, minValue, maxValue, lastValue), newest first. The window is the last 24 hours by default, and at most 30 days back, which is all the service keeps. An empty list means nothing changed in the window; currentHealthState then gives the state now. truncated means the answer stops before startTime: the hint says where. Find the model with amgmcp_query_resource_graph and resources | where type =~ 'microsoft.cloudhealth/healthmodels' | project id, name, resourceGroup, location, subscriptionId: the id column is healthModelId.

healthModelId.description: The model's Azure resource ID: the id column of amgmcp_query_resource_graph and resources | where type =~ 'microsoft.cloudhealth/healthmodels' | project id, name, resourceGroup, location, subscriptionId. It looks like /subscriptions/<id>/resourceGroups/<rg>/providers/Microsoft.CloudHealth/healthmodels/<name>.

entityName.description: The entity's name, as amgmcp_health_model_inspect gives it in entities[].name (not its displayName). The model's root entity has the model's name.

signalName.description: Optional. A signal's name, as amgmcp_health_model_inspect gives it in the entity's signals[].name. With it, the answer is that signal's values over time; without it, the entity's state changes.

startTime.description: Optional. Start of the window: RFC3339 (e.g. '2026-01-15T00:00:00Z') or relative (e.g. 'now-7d'). Default 24 hours before endTime. At most 30 days back.

endTime.description: Optional. End of the window: RFC3339 or relative (e.g. 'now-1h'). Default now.

annotations.title: Get Azure Monitor health model history

all.name: amgmcp_health_model_inspect
all.title: Inspect an Azure Monitor health model
all.description: Read an Azure Monitor health model as a graph: every entity's health state (Healthy, Degraded, Unhealthy or Unknown), its signals and the relationships along which states roll up from child to parent. Find the model with amgmcp_query_resource_graph and resources | where type =~ 'microsoft.cloudhealth/healthmodels' | project id, name, resourceGroup, location, subscriptionId: the id column is healthModelId. Each signal gives its latest state and value, its degradedRule and unhealthyRule, and what it measures: resourceId with metricNamespace and metricName (amgmcp_query_resource_metric), KQL in queryText on a Log Analytics workspace (amgmcp_query_resource_log), or PromQL in queryText on an Azure Monitor workspace (amgmcp_prometheus_query, with that workspace's resource ID as datasourceUid). To find why the root is not Healthy, follow the relationships down to the entities that are not Healthy, and read their signals. atTime shows the model as it was at a past time, to look into an incident. amgmcp_health_model_get_history gives the state changes and signal values over time. On a large model, signals can be left out (signalsOmitted, truncated): name the entities you need in entityNames.

healthModelId.description: The model's Azure resource ID: the id column of amgmcp_query_resource_graph and resources | where type =~ 'microsoft.cloudhealth/healthmodels' | project id, name, resourceGroup, location, subscriptionId. It looks like /subscriptions/<id>/resourceGroups/<rg>/providers/Microsoft.CloudHealth/healthmodels/<name>.

entityNames.description: Optional. Only these entities get their signals in the answer; every other entity keeps its name, state and place in the graph. Each must be an entity's name (not its displayName). Use it on a large model, or when the answer says signals were left out (signalsOmitted).

atTime.description: Optional. The model as it was at this time, to look into a past incident: RFC3339 (e.g. '2026-01-15T08:30:00Z') or relative (e.g. 'now-2h'). Leave it out for the model as it is now.

annotations.title: Inspect an Azure Monitor health model

all.name: amgmcp_kusto_get_metadata
all.title: Get Kusto metadata
all.description: Get the metadata of Azure Data Explorer (Kusto) clusters, as the signed-in user. With no arguments it lists the clusters the user can read in Azure, each with its clusterUrl; a cluster the user can query but not read in Azure is not listed, and clusterUrl takes it too. clusterUrl alone lists that cluster's databases, with each small database's schemaJson and table names for the large ones. clusterUrl and database return that database's full schema when it fits, otherwise 'tables' with each table's columns as 'name:type', otherwise table names only, plus 'functions' with each stored function's parameters - read that database's 'warning'. Add table to get only that table's columns, or a stored function's parameters and, when it takes no arguments, the columns it returns. Copy table and column names exactly as returned: Kusto names are case-sensitive.

clusterUrl.description: Optional Azure Data Explorer cluster, as its full address, such as https://help.kusto.windows.net or https://<cluster>.<region>.kusto.windows.net. Omit to list the clusters the user can read in Azure. A cluster the user can query but not read there works too. Anything but a cluster's URL fails with [invalid_argument], before any request.

database.description: Optional database name or pretty name, matched case-insensitively; it needs clusterUrl. A pretty name that several databases share matches none of them. Returns only that database, with more detail than clusterUrl alone: the full schema when it fits, otherwise 'tables' with each table's columns as 'name:type', otherwise table names only, and 'functions' with each stored function's parameters - read the database's 'warning'. A name the cluster lacks fails with [database_not_found] and lists its databases.

table.description: Optional table or stored function name, matched case-sensitively first and then case-insensitively; requires database. Returns only that table, its columns as 'name:type' in 'tables', instead of the whole database, which keeps a wide database's answer small. A stored function's name returns it in 'functions' with its parameters and, when it takes no arguments, the columns it returns in 'outputColumns'. A name that is both a table and a stored function describes the function, which is what a query naming it runs; the table is then reached as table('Name'). A name the database lacks comes back as the database's error, listing its tables and functions.

all.name: amgmcp_kusto_query
all.title: Query Kusto
all.description: Query data in an Azure Data Explorer (Kusto) cluster, as the signed-in user. clusterUrl names the cluster. Returns frame, metadata and hints: frame is the Grafana data frame (schema.fields + data.values, column-oriented; a dynamic column holds its JSON values, typed 'other'; a time column holds ISO 8601 UTC text); metadata has executedQuery, durationMs (how long the query ran), rowCount, totalRowCount (omitted when the row cap cut the result), truncated, truncationReason (max_rows or response_size), omittedColumnCount (columns left out of a very wide result) and warning (says when maxRows was changed or the row cap could not be added, and when a query with several result sets, such as fork, facet or two statements, returned only one of them, which truncated does not show) - read truncated and warning before treating the rows as complete, and aggregate or narrow the query rather than raising maxRows. A query that matches no rows returns rowCount 0 and an empty frame - schema.refId 'A', no fields and no values - not an error and not an empty response; metadata.executedQuery still says what ran. Before querying an unfamiliar database, get its exact table and column names with amgmcp_kusto_get_metadata, passing the same clusterUrl and database. The query is plain KQL: to run a dashboard panel's query, take toolCall.arguments from amgmcp_dashboard_inspect, which writes in the panel's variables and time range.

clusterUrl.description: The Azure Data Explorer cluster to query, as its full address, such as https://help.kusto.windows.net or https://<cluster>.<region>.kusto.windows.net. amgmcp_kusto_get_metadata lists the clusters the user can read in Azure; a cluster the user can query but not read there works too. Anything but a cluster's URL fails with [invalid_argument], before any request.

database.description: The Azure Data Explorer database name to query. A database the cluster does not have fails with [database_not_found] and lists its databases.

query.description: The Kusto query to execute. e.g. 'union * | limit 10' to explore 10 records to learn the data. Grafana macros and template variables ($__timeFilter, $__interval, $__rate_interval, ${var}, [[var]]) are not expanded: a call containing one is rejected with [unresolved_variable], so write literal times and values. In KQL a $__name inside a quoted string is plain text and is allowed (e.g. | where msg contains "$__interval"), except $__timeFilter, $__timeFrom, $__timeTo and $__timeInterval, which Azure Data Explorer replaces even there, also at the start of a longer name such as $__timeFromX; ${var} and [[var]] are refused there too. For a dashboard panel, amgmcp_dashboard_inspect returns the query ready to run in toolCall.arguments.

maxRows.description: Maximum rows to return (default 500, maximum 5000). A larger value is lowered to 5000, and metadata.warning says so. The query is capped at the source with '| take maxRows+1' appended, so Kusto sends at most one row past the cap and metadata.truncated is proven by that row; metadata.totalRowCount is then omitted, since the query's full row count is not read. Queries using render, fork or facet, with several result sets, or control commands other than .show run as written, and of several result sets only one comes back, as metadata.warning says. Rows also stop once their values pass about 40 KB (metadata.truncationReason response_size), and a column list over about 16 KB drops columns empty in every row, then trailing ones (metadata.omittedColumnCount, named in hints): project fewer columns, shorten long values or summarize.

all.name: amgmcp_prometheus_list_label_names
all.title: List Prometheus label names
all.description: List label names in a Prometheus datasource. Supports an optional time range (default: the last day); Azure Managed Prometheus does not implement the upstream match[] series-selector filter, so this tool does not expose it. Returns up to 'limit' labelNames plus totalCount and truncated, which is true when more label names exist than were returned; raise 'limit' to see the rest.

datasourceUid.description: The Azure Monitor workspace to query: its datasourceUid, p-<accountId>, as amgmcp_prometheus_list_workspaces gives it, or its Azure resource ID. A saved dashboard's Prometheus target names the same uid. A resource ID is looked up first, and the answer's datasourceUid gives the uid: pass that on later calls. Anything else fails with [invalid_argument], before any request.

startTime.description: Start time: RFC3339 (e.g. '2024-01-15T00:00:00Z') or relative expression (e.g. 'now-1h', 'now-7d').

endTime.description: End time: RFC3339 (e.g. '2024-01-16T00:00:00Z') or relative expression (e.g. 'now', 'now-1h').

limit.description: Max results to return. Must be greater than 0.

all.name: amgmcp_prometheus_list_metric_names
all.title: List Prometheus metric names
all.description: List metric names from a Prometheus datasource. Call this first to discover metrics before querying. Supports regex filtering and pagination. Returns metricNames for the requested page, totalCount (names matching the regex) and hasMore, which is true when a later page holds more names.

datasourceUid.description: The Azure Monitor workspace to query: its datasourceUid, p-<accountId>, as amgmcp_prometheus_list_workspaces gives it, or its Azure resource ID. A saved dashboard's Prometheus target names the same uid. A resource ID is looked up first, and the answer's datasourceUid gives the uid: pass that on later calls. Anything else fails with [invalid_argument], before any request.

regex.description: Regex to filter metric names. e.g. '.*cpu.*'.

limit.description: Max results to return. Must be greater than 0.

all.name: amgmcp_prometheus_list_workspaces
all.title: List Azure Monitor workspaces
all.description: List the Azure Monitor workspaces the signed-in user can read in Azure, by name, at most 200. Each workspace is a Prometheus data source: pass its datasourceUid to the other Prometheus tools. Each entry has datasourceUid, name, resourceId, subscriptionId, resourceGroup and location. truncated is true when more match than the list holds: narrow it with query or subscriptionIds. Reading a workspace's metrics takes a data role on it, such as Monitoring Data Reader, so a listed workspace can still refuse a query.

query.description: The words to find: a workspace matches when each word is in its name or resource group, or is its location. Several words can also spell the location, so 'West US 3' finds westus3. Leave it out to list every workspace.

subscriptionIds.description: Limit the list to these Azure subscription IDs (GUIDs, at most 500): one ID, a list, or IDs separated by commas. Leave it out to list every subscription the user can read. A subscription the user cannot read is skipped with no notice, and the call fails when the user can read none of them.

all.name: amgmcp_prometheus_query
all.title: Query Prometheus
all.description: WORKFLOW: amgmcp_prometheus_list_workspaces -> amgmcp_prometheus_list_metric_names -> amgmcp_prometheus_list_label_names -> amgmcp_prometheus_query. Query Prometheus using a PromQL expression. Supports range queries (startTime to endTime; startTime defaults to an hour before endTime) and instant queries (a single point evaluated at endTime, or now when endTime is omitted; startTime is not used, so omit it - warnings says so when one is passed more than 60 s from that time). Time formats: RFC3339 (e.g. '2026-01-01T00:00:00Z') or relative expressions like 'now', 'now-1h', 'now-30m'. The start-to-end span of a range query cannot exceed 32 days; Azure Managed Prometheus rejects wider ranges. A metric or label name with a dot must be quoted: {"system.cpu.time"}, or by ("service.name"). Azure Managed Prometheus allows only equality on a metric name, so the usual cardinality idiom count by (__name__) ({__name__!=""}) is rejected with 'Metric name only support equality(=) filter'. To find what is producing series, query the scrape statistics instead, e.g. topk(10, sum by (job, instance) (scrape_samples_scraped)).

datasourceUid.description: The Azure Monitor workspace to query: its datasourceUid, p-<accountId>, as amgmcp_prometheus_list_workspaces gives it, or its Azure resource ID. A saved dashboard's Prometheus target names the same uid. A resource ID is looked up first, and the answer's datasourceUid gives the uid: pass that on later calls. Anything else fails with [invalid_argument], before any request.

expr.description: The PromQL expression to evaluate (e.g. 'up', 'rate(http_requests_total[5m])'). Grafana macros and template variables ($__timeFilter, $__interval, $__rate_interval, ${var}, [[var]]) are not expanded: a call containing one is rejected with [unresolved_variable], so write literal times and values.

startTime.description: Start of a range query: RFC3339 (e.g. '2024-01-15T00:00:00Z') or relative expression (e.g. 'now-1h', 'now-7d'). Default: one hour before endTime. Not used by an instant query - omit it there.

endTime.description: End time: RFC3339 (e.g. '2024-01-16T00:00:00Z') or relative expression (e.g. 'now', 'now-1h').

stepSeconds.description: Step interval in seconds between data points for range queries (not used by instant queries). Defaults to 60s when omitted; specify for finer or coarser bucketing. Must be greater than 0. A range query returns at most 11,000 points per series, and Azure Managed Prometheus needs a step of at least 60s once the range exceeds 48 hours.

queryType.description: Query type: 'range' (default) returns values from startTime to endTime; 'instant' returns a single point evaluated at endTime (now when endTime is omitted). An instant query does not use startTime, so omit it: when one is passed and is more than 60 s from the evaluation time, the response's warnings say so.

all.name: amgmcp_query_activity_log
all.title: Query Azure activity log
all.description: Query Azure Activity Log to investigate management-plane operations (creates, deletes, updates, RBAC changes, deployments, etc.) on Azure resources. Returns at most 60 events; when more matched, nextLink is 'truncated' and comments says which part of the window the returned events cover and how to fetch the rest. No events does not prove nothing happened: Azure leaves out events the identity of the Azure Monitor data source cannot read, and answers a scope that does not exist with no events rather than an error.

scope.description: Azure scope for Activity Log query. Can be a subscription ('/subscriptions/{id}'), resource group ('/subscriptions/{id}/resourceGroups/{name}'), or a full resource ID.

startTime.description: Start time: RFC3339 (e.g. '2024-01-15T00:00:00Z') or relative expression (e.g. 'now-1h', 'now-7d').

endTime.description: End time: RFC3339 (e.g. '2024-01-16T00:00:00Z') or relative expression (e.g. 'now', 'now-1h').

correlationId.description: Optional correlation ID to filter activity log events. Works with any scope: Azure accepts a correlation ID only on its own, so the correlation's events are fetched for the whole subscription and then narrowed to the requested resource group or resource here. A resource scope also keeps events recorded on that resource's children (e.g. '.../vaults/x/accessPolicies/add'). No events means the correlation touched nothing in this scope; widen the scope to the subscription to see the rest of the correlation.

select.description: Optional comma-separated list of fields to return. Defaults to 'eventTimestamp,operationName,status,caller,resourceId,resourceGroupName,correlationId,level,description' to keep responses within the MCP size cap. Pass an explicit list (e.g. 'eventName,operationName,status,eventTimestamp,subStatus') to override; pass an empty string to fetch all fields. Fields not selected are omitted from each event. Azure attaches the caller's token 'claims' to every event whenever 'caller' is selected; they are dropped unless 'claims' is named here (or select is empty).

all.name: amgmcp_query_application_insights_trace
all.title: Query Application Insights trace
all.description: Query Application Insights Trace through Grafana Azure Monitor data source. When the trace data is stored in multiple Application Insights, this tool will aggregate the data. In each traceResults entry, fields with the same value in every item are moved out of the items into sameInAllItems, and customDimensions keys every item shares into sameInAllItems.customDimensions: an item is sameInAllItems merged with its own fields, customDimensions key by key. When every component searched answers and none has items for the operation id, the entries have empty traces and a note says what was searched and how to look further; when Application Insights reports an error for a search, the note quotes it. A component that cannot be queried at all is left out of traceResults.

operationId.description: operation ID (a.k.a 'operation_Id') for the Application Insights trace. The unique identifier of the root operation. This identifier allows grouping telemetry across multiple components. Pass the value itself, typically a 32-hex-digit W3C trace id or a GUID, though any custom id is accepted (e.g. 'order:12345'): at most 256 characters with no control characters, else it is rejected with [invalid_argument] before a query runs. It always reaches KQL as one escaped string literal. An id containing / \ ? # % + or & (old JavaScript SDK ids hold '/', pre-W3C .NET SDK ids '+'), or one that is just '.' or '..', is looked up in the given component only, with or without roughTimestamp, because the cross-component trace index cannot route it: query another component directly for telemetry it recorded.

roughTimestamp.description: Optional rough timestamp: RFC3339 (e.g. '2024-01-15T00:00:00Z') or relative expression (e.g. 'now-1h', 'now-7d'). If null, the given component's last 30 days are searched for an item of the operation, and the trace is read 10 hours either side of it. If provided, the trace is read 10 hours either side of this timestamp, so telemetry further from it is not returned.

all.name: amgmcp_query_azure_subscriptions
all.title: List Azure subscriptions
all.description: List all the Azure subscriptions that the identity of the Grafana Azure Monitor data source can access: the data source's own identity, such as a managed identity, or the signed-in user when the data source signs in as the user.

all.name: amgmcp_query_resource_graph
all.title: Query Azure Resource Graph
all.description: Query Azure Resource Graph (ARG) through Grafana Azure Monitor data source. e.g. 'resources | summarize count() by type' will groups all resources by their Azure resource type.

query.description: Azure Resource Graph query. e.g. 'resources | summarize count() by type' will groups all resources by their Azure resource type. Grafana macros and template variables ($__timeFilter, $__interval, $__rate_interval, ${var}, [[var]]) are not expanded: a call containing one is rejected with [unresolved_variable], so write literal times and values. In KQL a $__name inside a quoted string is plain text and is allowed (e.g. | where msg contains "$__interval"); ${var} and [[var]] are refused there too.

all.name: amgmcp_query_resource_health
all.title: Query Azure resource health
all.description: Query Azure Resource Health availability status for a subscription, resource group, or single resource. By default returns the current status for a single resource or current statuses for every child resource at sub/RG scope. Set includeHistory=true at resource scope to return historical availability transitions. Optionally expands recommendedActions.

scope.description: Azure scope: a subscription ('/subscriptions/{id}'), resource group ('/subscriptions/{id}/resourceGroups/{name}'), or full resource ID.

includeHistory.description: When true and scope is a single resource, returns historical availability transitions instead of the current status. Ignored at subscription or resource-group scope (always list mode).

expandRecommendedActions.description: When true, expands the recommendedActions[] array in each returned status. Adds $expand=recommendedactions.

filter.description: Optional OData $filter. Example: "properties/availabilityState eq 'Unavailable'". Applied at subscription and resource-group scope. NOT supported for a single resource's current status — ARM's per-resource endpoint ignores it, so the tool rejects that combination rather than returning a status that may contradict the filter; read availabilityState from the response instead, or set includeHistory=true to filter that resource's historical transitions.

all.name: amgmcp_query_resource_health_events
all.title: Query Azure resource health events
all.description: Query Azure Resource Health service-health events (service issues, planned maintenance, health advisories, security advisories, RCAs, emerging issues, billing events) at subscription or single-resource scope. Resource-group scope is not supported by the ARM API; query at subscription scope and narrow via the filter parameter. Returns a triage-sized view by default — the long-form narrative fields (description, summary, article, faqs, recommendedActions) are omitted unless includeEventDetails=true, and results are capped at 200 events with nextLink='truncated' when more matched. Note that startTime has date granularity only, so it cannot express a window narrower than one day, and ARM applies it to each event's LAST UPDATE time rather than to when impact began or whether the event is still active — an incident that is still Active but has not been updated inside the window is excluded. It defaults to a 30-day look-back at subscription scope. impactStartTime is NOT filterable, so do not try to narrow with it; filter fields need the 'properties/' prefix, e.g. "properties/status eq 'Active'" to keep only live incidents.

scope.description: Azure scope: a subscription ('/subscriptions/{id}') or a full resource ID. Resource groups are not supported — query at subscription scope and narrow via the filter parameter.

startTime.description: Start of the look-back window: RFC3339 (e.g. '2026-01-15T00:00:00Z') or relative expression (e.g. 'now-7d', 'now-30d'). IMPORTANT: ARM applies this window to each event's LAST UPDATE time, not to when its impact began and not to whether it is still active. An incident that is still Active but has not been updated inside the window is excluded, so a narrow window can report zero events while an outage is ongoing. Widen the window if you are looking for current incidents, and use "properties/status eq 'Active'" in filter to keep only live ones. ARM accepts DATE granularity only here, so the time of day is discarded: any value falling inside today ('now-1h', 'now-6h') resolves to 'since 00:00 UTC today', and one day is the narrowest window this parameter can express. Honored only at subscription scope; the tool rejects this at resource scope with an explicit error. When omitted at subscription scope, defaults to a 30-day look-back.

filter.description: Optional OData $filter. Fields need the 'properties/' prefix — a bare field name is rejected with InvalidODataQueryOptions. Verified working: "properties/status eq 'Active'", "properties/eventType eq 'ServiceIssue'", and the two combined with 'and'. Use "properties/status eq 'Active'" to keep only live incidents. Note impactStartTime is NOT filterable here (ARM rejects it in both bare and properties/ form) — bound the window with startTime instead, remembering that startTime filters on last-update time rather than impact time.

includeEventDetails.description: When false (default), the long-form narrative fields are omitted from each event — description, summary, header, article, faqs, recommendedActions, links, additionalInformation, and the per-region impact[].impactedRegions[].updates[] communication log — so the response stays inside the MCP response-size cap. Triage fields (title, status, level, eventType, impactStartTime, impactMitigationTime, tracking id, and impact[] down to impacted service, region and per-region status) are always returned. Set true to get the full ARM payload for the matched events; on a busy subscription or a wide window that can exceed the size cap and fail the call, so narrow with filter first.

all.name: amgmcp_query_resource_log
all.title: Query Azure resource logs (including Application Insights and Log Analytics)
all.description: Query Azure Resource Log through Grafana Azure Monitor data source

query.description: Kusto Query Language (KQL) query to execute against the resource logs. For Log Analytics workspaces and most Azure resources, 'union * | limit 10' explores the schema and the time column is 'TimeGenerated'. For Application Insights components, the time column is 'timestamp' (lowercase); prefer a named-table union like 'union requests, dependencies, exceptions, traces, customEvents | take 10' to keep response size down — 'union *' also works but pulls every table. IMPORTANT: this tool sends NO time window. The query must carry its own time filter (e.g. | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)), or it runs unbounded. When re-running a query copied out of a dashboard panel, replace its macros with a literal ago(...) or between(...) filter that covers the dashboard's time range. Grafana macros and template variables ($__timeFilter, $__interval, $__rate_interval, ${var}, [[var]]) are not expanded: a call containing one is rejected with [unresolved_variable], so write literal times and values. In KQL a $__name inside a quoted string is plain text and is allowed (e.g. | where msg contains "$__interval"); ${var} and [[var]] are refused there too.

annotations.title: Query Azure resource logs (including Application Insights and Log Analytics)

all.name: amgmcp_query_resource_metric
all.title: Query Azure resource metrics
all.description: Query Azure Resource Metric values for one or more resources (up to 100) through Grafana Azure Monitor data source. Multiple resources are queried in parallel. Supports comma-separated metric names (max 20) in a single call to reduce ARM request count.

azureResourceId.description: One or more Azure Resource IDs, separated by commas. Maximum 100 resource IDs. e.g. '/subscriptions/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000/resourceGroups/rg1/providers/Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/sa1,/subscriptions/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000/resourceGroups/rg2/providers/Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/sa2'

metricName.description: The metric name(s) to query. Supports comma-separated values for multiple metrics in a single call (max 20). e.g., 'BlobCount' or 'Percentage CPU,Available Memory Bytes,Network In Total'. Use 'amgmcp_query_resource_metric_definition' to get available metrics for a resource.

startTime.description: Start time: RFC3339 (e.g. '2024-01-15T00:00:00Z') or relative expression (e.g. 'now-1h', 'now-7d').

endTime.description: End time: RFC3339 (e.g. '2024-01-16T00:00:00Z') or relative expression (e.g. 'now', 'now-1h').

filter.description: Optional OData filter to apply to the metric query. e.g., 'BlobType eq "BlockBlob"'. A wildcard such as "VMName eq '*'" SPLITS the result into one time series per dimension value — and Azure Monitor then returns only the top 10 series by value unless you raise 'top'. With a 20-instance scale set that means half the fleet is missing and the returned series sum to about half the unsplit total, with nothing in the response marking the omission, so set 'top' whenever you split and intend to enumerate or sum.

aggregation.description: Aggregation type for the metric. Valid values: 'Average', 'Count', 'Maximum', 'Minimum', 'Total'. Azure Monitor rejects an unsupported aggregation on some metrics (errorCode 'InvalidSamplingType') but on others computes it anyway and returns 'Success', so a wrong choice can yield a plausible number instead of an error. 'Total' on a gauge (a point-in-time level such as UsedCapacity, a percentage, or a queue depth) sums the samples in the window: UsedCapacity over 7 days returned ~30.7 TB as Total against ~182 GB as Average — a 168x overstatement, in Bytes, reported as a success. Use 'Total' only for metrics that accumulate (Transactions, Ingress, request counts). When unsure, check supportedAggregationTypes and primaryAggregationType via amgmcp_query_resource_metric_definition.

interval.description: Time interval (timegrain) for the metric aggregation in ISO 8601 duration format. Defaults to 'PT1H' (1 hour) when omitted. Examples: 'PT1M' for 1 minute, 'PT1H' for 1 hour. Use the special value 'FULL' to get a single datapoint for the entire time span.

top.description: Maximum number of time series to return per resource when 'filter' splits by a dimension. Azure Monitor defaults to 10 and orders series descending by value, so omitting this silently drops every series past the tenth — set it above the number of dimension values you expect (e.g. the instance count of a scale set) when you need the complete split. Ignored when 'filter' does not split.

all.name: amgmcp_query_resource_metric_definition
all.title: Query Azure resource metric definitions
all.description: Query Azure Resource Metric Definitions through Grafana Azure Monitor data source. azureResourceId must be an individual resource; a subscription or resource-group id is rejected with [invalid_argument] (find the resources in it with amgmcp_query_resource_graph).

all.name: appconfig_account_list
all.title: List App Configuration Stores
all.description:
List all App Configuration stores in a subscription. This command retrieves and displays all App Configuration
stores available in the specified subscription. Results include store names returned as a JSON array.

tenant.description: The Microsoft Entra ID tenant GUID identifier or display name.

subscription.description: The Azure subscription GUID identifier or display name. If not specified, the Azure CLI profile default subscription or AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID environment variable will be used.

all.name: appconfig_kv_delete
all.title: Delete App Configuration Key-Value Setting
all.description:
Delete a key-value pair from an App Configuration store. This command removes the specified key-value pair from the store.
If a label is specified, only the labeled version is deleted. If no label is specified, the key-value with the matching
key and the default label will be deleted.

account.description: The name of the App Configuration store (e.g., my-appconfig).

key.description: The name of the key to access within the App Configuration store.

label.description: The label to apply to the configuration key. Labels are used to group and organize settings.

tenant.description: The Microsoft Entra ID tenant GUID identifier or display name.

subscription.description: The Azure subscription GUID identifier or display name. If not specified, the Azure CLI profile default subscription or AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID environment variable will be used.

all.name: appconfig_kv_get
all.title: Gets App Configuration Key-Value Settings
all.description:
Gets key-values in an App Configuration store. This command can either retrieve a specific key-value by its key
and optional label, or list key-values if no key is provided. Listing key-values can optionally be filtered by a
key filter and label filter. Each key-value includes its key, value, label, content type, ETag, last modified time,
and lock status.

account.description: The name of the App Configuration store (e.g., my-appconfig).

key.description: The name of the key to access within the App Configuration store.

all.name: arm_create_or_update_resource
all.title: Create or Update Azure Resource
all.description:
Performs a PUT operation for a single Azure resource. This can be used to create or update a resource.
    It should be provided with the scope of this resource deployment. This can either be management group for management group-scoped resources, 
    subscription for subscription-scoped resources, tenant for tenant-scoped resources, or resource group for resource group-scoped resources. The resource type and it's name should also be provided,

    for example by using the GetResourceTypeSchema tool to understand the required properties for the resource and then generating a compliant resource definition.

    This tool is used to:
    - Create or update a single Azure resource when you have the full resource definition ready and want to deploy it directly without using an ARM template deployment. 
    This can be useful for quick deployments or updates of individual resources.

    For example, given the prompt "Create a storage account in my resource group", this tool can be used to create the storage account.

    Other prompts which would highly qualify for using this tool include:
    - "Create a new subnet in my subscription, under myVnet"
    - "Setup a VMSS in my subscription?"
    - "Create an AAD application in my tenant"

request.description: The request details for the single resource PUT operation.

all.name: arm_execute_query
all.title: Execute Azure Resource Graph Query
all.description:
Execute an Azure Resource Graph query, and return the results. The query can be used to fetch information about Azure resources.
This tool is used to:
- Run Azure Resource Graph (ARG) queries to retrieve real-time data about your Azure resources
- Support pagination and handling of large result sets through the use of `skipToken`
- Provide insights into resource inventory, configuration, and relationships at scale

Recommended workflow: first call `generate_query` from a natural language prompt, then call `validate_query` on the generated query, and only then call `execute_query`.

Important: query execution may return truncated or paginated results. After executing, always check for a `skipToken`; when present, call `execute_query` again with that token to retrieve additional pages. Treat answers as non-conclusive until no `skipToken` is returned.

For example, executing the following query:

```kusto
Resources
| where type == "microsoft.compute/virtualmachines"
| project name, location, resourceGroup
```

Returns a response with the matching virtual machines, a `rowCount`, and optionally a `skipToken` if there are more results. Pass the `skipToken` in the `options.$skipToken` field of the next call to page through remaining results:

```json
{"isSuccessful":true,"results":{"}
    {
    "isSuccessful": true,
    "results": {
        "$id": "1",
        "data": [
        {
            "name": "",
            "location": "",
            "resourceGroup": ""
        },
        ...
        ],
        "facets": []
    },
    "rowCount": <x>,
    "executedQuery": "Resources\n| where type == \"microsoft.compute/virtualmachines\"\n| project name, location, resourceGroup",
    "totalRecords": <y>>,
    "resultTruncated": false,
    "skipToken": "<skipToken>"
    }
```

query.description: The Azure Resource Graph query to execute.

options.description: Optional query execution parameters and settings such as pagination, result format, and scoping options.

$top.description: The maximum number of rows that the query should return. Overrides the page size when $skipToken property is present.

$skipToken.description: Continuation token for pagination, capturing the next page size and offset, as well as the context of the query.

resultFormat.description: Defines in which format query result returned.

all.name: arm_execute_resource_action
all.title: Invoke Azure Resource Action
all.description:
Performs a POST action on a single Azure resource. It should be provided with the scope of the target resource. This can be a management group for
    management group-scoped resources, subscription for subscription-scoped resources, tenant for tenant-scoped resources, resource group for resource
    group-scoped resources, or resource for extension resources. The provider namespace, resource type and name segments, API version, and action name
    should also be provided, along with optional query parameters and an optional action request body. Query parameter names should not include '?', '&' or '=',
    values should not be pre-escaped, and api-version must be supplied using the dedicated API version field. Use the ListResourceAndActionTypes and
    GetResourceActionSchema tools ahead of time to discover Bicep-indexed actions and generate a compliant request body. Omitting the body sends no HTTP
    request content; provide an empty object only when the action explicitly expects one.

    This tool is used to:
    - Invoke an action on an existing Azure resource when the action is exposed as a POST operation, such as restarting, starting, validating, or retrieving
    resource-specific information that is not available through a standard resource GET operation.

    For example, given the prompt "Restart my virtual machine named vm1 in resource group rg1", this tool can be used to invoke the restart action on the VM.

    Other prompts which would highly qualify for using this tool include:
    - "Start the virtual machine named vm1 in my resource group"
    - "List the access keys for my storage account"
    - "Validate this deployment before creating it"

    Actions may mutate resources or return sensitive values such as access keys. Confirm the exact target resource and action before invoking this tool,
    and do not expose sensitive response values unnecessarily.

request.description: The resource action request, including the target resource, action name, API version, optional query parameters, and optional body.

all.name: arm_generate_query
all.title: Generate Azure Resource Graph Query
all.description:
Generate an Azure Resource Graph query from a natural language prompt. The generated query can be used to fetch real-time information about your Azure estate.

This tool is used to:
- Translate intent (natural language) into a valid Azure Resource Graph (ARG) query.
- Investigate current Azure inventory, configuration, and resource relationships at scale.
- Prepare queries for validation and execution workflows.

This query can be supplied to the `validate_query` tool to verify the syntax, and the `execute_query` tool to run it and return results.

Recommended workflow: first call `generate_query` from a natural language prompt, then call `validate_query` on the generated query, and only then call `execute_query`.

For example, given the prompt "List all virtual machines", a generated query might be:

```kusto
Resources
| where type == "microsoft.compute/virtualmachines"
| project name, location, resourceGroup
```

prompt.description: Natural language input used to generate an Azure Resource Graph query for real-time visibility into your Azure estate.

all.name: arm_get_async_operation_status
all.title: Get ARM Async Operation Status
all.description:
Used to poll the status of a long-running ARM operation until the operation is complete.
    This applies to these tools when they return a response with a "locationHeaderUrl" field and a 200, 201 or 202 status code:
    - create_or_update_resource (e.g. creating a storage account, VM, or any resource that provisions asynchronously)
    - execute_resource_action (e.g. restarting a virtual machine)
    - delete_resource (when the resource is deleted asynchronously)
    - whatif_deployment (when the what-if analysis takes longer to compute)
    
    Do not use this tool for create_deployment responses. For deployments, always use get_deployment_status instead.
    
    Pass the full URL from the "locationHeaderUrl" field of the initial response directly to this tool.
    If the operation is still in progress, a 202 response will be returned — call this tool again until a terminal status (200 with result) is received.

    Judging completion:
    - Initial result of a mutating call: if it has no "locationHeaderUrl" field, the operation is already complete and must not be polled.
    - Azure-AsyncOperation polling response: judge it by its top-level "status" field, not by the absence of a "locationHeaderUrl" field.
      A 200 carrying a non-terminal "status" such as "InProgress" means the operation is still running — keep calling this tool with the
      original polling URL until "status" is "Succeeded", "Failed" or "Canceled".
    - Resource re-read: judge it by "properties.provisioningState" reaching a terminal value.

    A response whose "locationHeaderUrl" is null is still in progress but supplied no polling URL; in that case read the
    resource directly with get_resource until its provisioningState reaches a terminal value, and consult the
    "contractWarning" field for the reason.

    Wait for the number of seconds given by the "retryAfterSeconds" field of the most recent response before each retry.
    That value comes from the service and reflects how long the operation is expected to need, so honour it rather than polling on a fixed interval.

locationHeaderUrl.description: The full URL from the locationHeaderUrl field returned by the initial async operation.

all.name: arm_get_deployment_status
all.title: Get ARM Template Deployment Status
all.description:
Used to get the current status of an ARM template deployment. This tool should only be called for deployments created with the create_deployment tool and can be used to check the progress of a deployment, see if it has completed successfully, or if there are any errors.
It takes the subscriptionId, resource group name, and deployment name as input to identify which deployment's status to retrieve. This tool can either be called on demand 
or called every 30 seconds after initiating a deployment to monitor its status until completion.

request.description: Deployment details to identify which deployment's status to retrieve.

all.name: arm_get_pricesheet_status
all.title: Get Pricesheet Download Status
all.description:
Poll the pricesheet download operation status URL returned by start_pricesheet_download.
Returns InProgress (with retryAfterSeconds) or Succeeded (with downloadUrl SAS link, valid ~1 hour).
The MCP server does NOT fetch the blob — pass the downloadUrl back to the user / agent client.
Security: only management.azure.com URLs are accepted.

operationStatusUrl.description: Operation status URL returned by start_pricesheet_download (must be on management.azure.com).

all.name: arm_get_resource
all.title: Get Azure Resource
all.description:
Performs a GET operation for a single Azure resource and returns its current ARM representation.
    Provide the exact resource ID from the resource's 'id' property. If apiVersion is omitted, the latest
    available API version for the resource type is used. Tracked, proxy and extension resources are all supported.

    Some GET APIs - particularly proxy and extension resources such as Microsoft.Insights/metrics - require additional
    query parameters. Supply those through the optional queryParameters field, not on the resource ID. Query parameter
    names must not include '?', '&' or '=', values must not be pre-escaped, and api-version must be supplied using the
    dedicated apiVersion field.

    Use this tool when you already have the full resource ID and need the resource's properties directly
    from Azure Resource Manager. Use Azure Resource Graph tools first when the resource ID is not known.

resourceId.description: The Azure resource ID to retrieve, using the exact value of the resource's 'id' property. Use an absolute ARM path beginning with '/'. Do not provide a management.azure.com URL or include query parameters such as api-version.

apiVersion.description: API version value. E.g. 2025-01-03. If not provided, the latest api-version for the resource type will be used.

queryParameters.description: Optional query parameters to append to the GET request, as a name/value map. E.g. {"$filter": "Tier eq '*'", "metricnames": "BlobCount,BlobCapacity"}. Do not include 'api-version' here and do not URL-encode the values.

all.name: arm_get_resource_action_schema
all.title: Get Azure Resource Action Schema
all.description:
Retrieves the JSON schema for the request body of a resource action (e.g. listAccountSas, listKeys) exposed by a given Azure resource type and API version.
Resource actions are POST operations invoked on a resource - such as listing account keys or generating a SAS token - rather than the resource's PUT/GET body.
If the action does not require a request body (e.g. listKeys), an empty object schema is returned.
Use the list_resource_and_action_types tool first to discover which actions are available for a resource type at a given API version.

apiVersion.description: The API version of the resource (e.g., '2023-01-01')

actionName.description: The name of the resource action (e.g., 'listKeys')

all.name: arm_get_resource_type_schema
all.title: Get Azure Resource Type Schema
all.description: Retrieves the JSON schema for a given Azure resource type and API version. This can be used to understand the required and optional properties for a resource when authoring ARM templates or making direct ARM API calls.

apiVersion.description: The API version of the resource (e.g., '2024-11-01')

all.name: arm_get_retail_prices
all.title: Get Azure Retail Prices
all.description:
Look up Azure retail (public/pay-as-you-go) pricing for any service, SKU, and region.
No Azure authentication needed — this queries the public Azure Retail Prices API.
Filter by service name, SKU, region, meter name, and price type.
Returns the raw response from the Retail Prices API. Top-level fields include
'Items' (array of price records — each with retailPrice, unitPrice, meterId, productName,
skuName, armSkuName, armRegionName, serviceName, serviceFamily, unitOfMeasure, type,
effectiveStartDate, etc.), 'Count', and 'NextPageLink' when more results exist.
Example: "How much does a Standard_D4s_v5 VM cost in East US?"

serviceName.description: Service name (e.g., 'Virtual Machines', 'Storage', 'SQL Database', 'Azure Cosmos DB')

meterName.description: Meter name to search for (e.g., 'D4s v5', 'P30 Disk')

all.name: arm_list_resource_and_action_types
all.title: List Azure Resource and Action Types
all.description:
Retrieves the available resource types and their latest API versions, along with any resource actions (e.g. listKeys, listAccountSas) 
available for each resource type at that API version, that can be used in ARM templates as well as individual calls to ARM. 
This tool can be used to discover which resource types are available for deployment, what the latest API version is for each type, 
and which POST actions can be invoked on a given resource type, helping users author ARM templates and direct ARM API calls with up-to-date resource and action information.

Pass the optional 'resourceType' parameter whenever the resource type is already known - the response is then scoped to that single type and
lists only the actions available for it, instead of returning the full catalog and the actions of every resource type. This keeps the
response small and avoids picking an action that belongs to a different resource type. Supply the full path, either a top-level type such as
'Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts' or a nested (child) type such as 'Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/blobServices/containers'.

This tool is used to:
- Discover available resource types for deployment.
- Determine the latest API version for each resource type.
- Discover available actions (e.g. listKeys) that can be invoked on a resource type.

resourceType.description: Optional. A fully qualified resource type used to scope the response to that type and its actions only. Nested (child) types are supported - supply the full path, e.g. 'Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts' or 'Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/blobServices/containers'. Omit to list every resource type.

annotations.title: List Azure Resource and Action Types

all.name: arm_query_aks_costs
all.title: Query AKS Costs
all.description:
Query AKS (Azure Kubernetes Service) container-level cost data, broken down by Cluster, Namespace,
UtilizationBucket (Idle/Service/System/Unallocated), ServiceCategory (Compute/Storage/Network), and more.
Subscription scope ONLY — exact shape /subscriptions/{subscriptionId} (no resource-group, billing-account, or MG scopes).
Defaults to MonthToDate. Lookback capped at ~3 months. Returns up to 100 rows (hard cap).
If a user request spans more than ~10 subscriptions, ask the user to narrow scope first (the upstream Cost Management API is throttled).
Supported dimensions: Cost, CostUSD, Currency, UsageDate, ResourceLocation, ServiceCategory,
UtilizationBucket, ResourceId, ResourceName, Meter, Cluster (level 0), Namespace (level 1).

scope.description: Subscription scope, e.g., /subscriptions/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000. Resource group / billing scopes are NOT supported.

timeframe.description: Time period: MonthToDate (default), TheLastMonth, WeekToDate, or Custom. Use 'Custom' together with from/to.

from.description: Start date (YYYY-MM-DD). Required together with 'to'. Supplying from/to auto-selects timeframe='Custom'.

to.description: End date (YYYY-MM-DD). Required together with 'from'. Supplying from/to auto-selects timeframe='Custom'.
